lines: Industrial designer John Mauriello argues design has abandoned its humanist roots for a sterile minimalism driven by corporate efficiency, producing products that meet metrics but evoke little desire or meaning.

He says profit-driven design aims at the 'barely good enough' threshold to cut manufacturing complexity, homogenizing products; he reads the spread of screens in cars as cost optimization that removes mechanical interfaces rather than a user-centric advance.
The episode links low-rate environments to founders prioritizing storytelling over working products, citing Theranos as a narrative that collapsed against physical and scientific reality.

Mauriello contrasts this with Steve Jobs, arguing real innovation pairs ambitious vision with setting ego aside to listen to engineers on technical constraints, and that reclaiming design means putting human needs ahead of extractive scale.
title: Why Nothing Looks Cool Anymore | John Mauriello
